newsitem.title: USA: Cosby struggles to cope with son's murder.
newsitem.headline: Cosby struggles to cope with son's murder.

text.p: Entertainer Bill Cosby is struggling hard to cope with the loss of his only son, killed last week by an unidentified gunman who has eluded a massive police manhunt.

"Your concentration goes in 18 different directions," a grieving Cosby told his publicist and longtime friend David Brokaw this weekend. "You try to pull things back together but it's like playing with oil and water."

But even while in seclusion somewhere in the eastern United States, the famed comedian was reaching out to comfort a Los Angeles mother whose teenage daughter was killed by gunfire only hours after 27-year-old Ennis Cosby was gunned down along a freeway.

Both killers were still at large on Sunday, but investigators were hoping for a breakthrough in the Cosby case as they circulated a composite sketch of their suspect -- a white man with a menacing stare wearing a knit cap.

Enlisting the public's help in solving a murder that has shocked the nation, police said the drawing was put together from the description provided by a woman who witnessed part of the attack early on Thursday morning.

The woman, a 47-year-old screenwriter, was said to be a friend who came to help Cosby change a flat tire. When a man with a pistol accosted them, she fled the scene in fear, only to return and find Cosby lying dead next to his Mercedes convertible, a source close to the investigation said.
The killer was described as being of average height and weight and between the ages of 25 and 32. Investigators said he was on foot and that robbery was his likely motive.

Police also released a drawing of a possible witness -- a white man in his late 20s or early 30s with a moustache and goatee wearing a dark beret. He may have been driving past at the time of the roadside killing but has yet to come forward.
"The Cosby family extends their hearts and deep appreciation to those who have come forward to help lighten the load of the Los Angeles Police Department," they said in a written statement.
After talking to Cosby late on Saturday, his publicist said he seemed "very composed and focused, but it's hard for any of us to imagine what he's dealing with inside."
Even while grieving in private, Cosby took time to phone the mother of a 17-year-old girl who was killed by a gang member while riding a city bus in Los Angeles on Thursday.

In a message left on his publicist's answering machine, Cosby challenged tabloid publications and TV shows to offer a reward for information on the killer instead of using their money to buy exclusives.

"It's the tabloids," Cosby said. "They're looking for something and they pay money for pictures. They pay money to have witnesses talk and it disrupts the case. Why can't the tabloids put out the word ... that they would pay to have someone come forward, and they could have exclusivity of the story."

In San Francisco, Martin Luther King III, son of the slain civil rights leader, said: "When I was a small child, Bill Cosby came to my home to comfort my brother and I when my father was gunned down. And to see almost 30 years later his son being gunned down, it's very tragic."
Ennis Cosby was the model for Cosby's TV son Theo in the popular NBC series "The Cosby Show," which ran from 1984 to 1992 and cemented its star's position as one of America's best-loved comedians.
